STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is about 26 cm across (dinner plate size). Its usable area is roughly 22 x 22 cm, so about 480 cm^2 for the rim-to-rim footprint; using the circular formula for a 26 cm plate gives 530 cm^2. I'll use ~500 cm^2 as the vessel area.

STEP 3 - Items: Roasted/fried potato pieces (cubes and wedges, golden-brown, some crispy edges). No visible oil pool or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: The potato pieces cover roughly 30% of the plate, clustered in the upper-right half, with one piece on the left.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut, roasted potato pieces have bulk density around 0.6 g/ml. 225 ml x 0.6 ≈ 135 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted/fried potato is about 130-150 kcal per 100 g. Using 140 kcal/100 g: 135 g x 1.4 ≈ 189 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 13-15 pieces of potato, roughly 135 g, is a plausible side-dish portion for what is visible. The estimate is consistent with the picture.
